LEARNING PATH LESSON · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Welcome, Include, Cooperate & Teamwork — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson takes kindness public: the four words that turn a group of children into a team, starting with the door (welcome) and ending with the cheer (teamwork).

What is this?

Welcome, include, cooperate and teamwork are the four group words: welcome greets the newcomer, include opens the circle wider, cooperate gives everyone a part and teamwork is the warm feeling when all the parts work.

What does it mean?

Classrooms and playgrounds run on these four words — the child who can welcome, include and cooperate becomes a social hub, and social hubs are looked up to, not left out.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three ideas: welcome is a HELLO plus a smile (it takes ten seconds); include means scanning for the one standing alone (the advanced move); and cooperate means everybody does a PART — nobody does everything.

Why this matters

This card turns all the private kindness of the earlier cards outward. Kindness to a friend is love; kindness to a stranger is leadership — and four-year-olds can lead.

What it teaches

Social inclusion behaviours, cooperative play (the developmental step beyond parallel play), task division, and group belonging — the feeling of being part of a we.

Words to learn

welcomeincludecooperateteamworktogetherpartgroup

Say this to your child

“"Groups are made of words. Welcome — hi, come in, we are glad you came. Include — you can play too; there is always room in a kind circle. Cooperate — we each take a part: you hold, I build, she finds the pieces. And teamwork — that is the feeling when it all works, the one that makes you shout WE DID IT with your whole body. Here is a secret: the strongest kids in any classroom are not the loudest — they are the ones who say you can play too."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "Four words that build a team."
  2. Read the panels: the waving boy WELCOMES, the open-armed girl INCLUDES, the ready boy is set to COOPERATE, and the two children arm in arm are TEAMWORK.
  3. Rehearse the hello: practise three welcomes — big wave, quiet smile, silly bow — all three count.
  4. Play the inclusion scan: "look around the playground in your mind — who is standing alone? What could we say?"
  5. Close with the fort mission below and the takeaway: "many hands, one team — and everybody does a part."

Look closer at the picture

On this card four panels build the team: Welcome, a waving boy; Include, a girl with her arms open wide; Cooperate, a smiling boy ready to pitch in; and Teamwork, two children with their arms around each other — the group words drawn at playground size.

Ask your child

"What does welcome sound like?" "What could we say to someone playing alone?" "What does cooperate mean — everyone does everything, or everyone does a part?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "You can play too!" "I will hold it, you build" or the proud one: "we did TEAMWORK!"

Out in the real world

Group moments fill the week: the new child at swimming lessons, the cousin visit, the puzzle that needs four hands, the cooking where one stirs and one pours. Name the roles out loud — "you welcome, I wash, she stirs — teamwork!" — and the words become reflexes.

Try it together

The Four-Hands Fort: a mission only possible as a team — a sofa-cushion fort that needs one holder, one builder, one fetcher and one inspector (rotate roles every five minutes). Halfway through, a stuffed animal arrives "new" and must be WELCOMED and INCLUDED with a job. Finish with the team cheer and the debrief: which word did the work?

Understanding check

Ask: "Which word opens the circle? Which word gives everyone a part? What do we shout when it works?" Include, cooperate, teamwork — three answers and the team words are live.

Parent tips

Assign inclusion as a job, not a virtue: "you are our Welcomer today — watch for anyone who needs a hello." Jobs feel doable where values feel vague. And when the squabbles come mid-build (they will), that is cooperate practice, not failure — teams negotiate.

This lesson pairs with the Welcome, Include, Cooperate & Teamwork flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Feelings & Kindness (Class 38).
